annotations.text: Every board has a light / dark chip above it — the whole app is themed from one token set, so flip any board to see it in dark mode. Row 1: the landing page (front door, pre-login) and the two phone screens.

Phone: full parity now, all seven mobile screens. The 5-item bottom tab bar (Overview/Approvals/Strategies/Backtest/Insights) covers primary nav; History and Settings — not in the tab bar, no room for a 6th — are reached via two small icons in the header instead (visible on every phone screen), so no screen is more than one tap from either. Approve/Reject stay full-width thumb targets everywhere; tables become stacked cards (History); sliders become compact value rows (Settings); dense desktop content (Backtest's trade list, Insights' Ask panel) is trimmed to what's actually useful on a 390px screen, not squeezed in 1:1.
Desktop app: Overview is the in-app home. Approvals · Strategies · Backtest · Insights · History · Settings share the same nav, now with two more icons for the pages below.

Phase 1 of the UI rebuild: Overview now shows a per-strategy ("Book") performance strip so strategies are comparable at a glance, not just an aggregate number. Approvals adds a Notify-threshold badge per signal (was it worth pushing to your phone?), a low-friction optional note field for the trade journal, and an "Always manual" badge on Volatility Harvester's add-to-a-losing-position action, which can never be auto-approved.

Phase 2: Strategies now lists all five (was two), each tagged trading/investment style. Its detail panel gets a Notify-threshold slider alongside the auto-approve one, plus a "View full details →" link into the new Strategy detail drill-in (bottom-right, next to Backtest-compare) — plain-English explanation, current parameters with what each one controls, and a version changelog showing backtested performance before/after each change.

New this pass, answering "what's missing to feel complete": History (full trade log, filterable, exportable — your ISA record) and Settings (risk limits, notification toggles, kill-switch panel, account status) are full nav destinations. Onboarding is the actual front door the Landing page's button now leads to. Phase 4: Insights (below) now has a "Today's briefing" digest above the per-signal list, a Screening tag on each signal (the cheap tier that runs on everything — a deeper research tier for candidates that clear the quant screen is a near-term fast-follow, not v1), and the top signal shows its trigger marked directly on a small price chart instead of only in text.

Phase 3: History's Status/Outcome columns now cover every decision, not just executed trades — a rejected or expired signal shows its counterfactual outcome ("would have: −£11.20") right next to real ones, plus your journal note. A new "Your calls, in hindsight" tile scores whether your own approve/reject judgment is adding value.

Phase 5: Settings' Notifications card now shows both channels — Push (this device) and Email, each event still toggled individually — and the Account card gains an "Installed on this device" row confirming the PWA is set up. This is account-wide notification plumbing; which specific signals actually push is still set per strategy on the Strategies page (its Notify threshold slider).

Performance, Instrument and Backtest-compare are drill-in pages, not top-level nav items — reached via a breadcrumb (e.g. "Strategies / Compare performance") from wherever they're relevant, the way a real app would route them rather than crowding the main nav further.

Phase 3: Compare performance now covers all five strategies plus the benchmark (was two), adds Sharpe and profit factor next to win rate and drawdown, and a correlation matrix — a strategy with a great return that just tracks another one isn't really diversifying you.

Phase 4: Backtest gets a Config version selector (v3 current / v2 / start a new draft) and the strategy list covers all five. Saved runs are now labelled by the version they tested, not just a nickname — so "which version is this" is never ambiguous.

Phase 4: Compare backtest runs now shows the actual parameter diff between versions ("Loss limit −2.5% → −2.0%") right on each card, not just prose — this is the concrete moment a candidate version either becomes the new baseline or doesn't, feeding straight into the version changelog on the Strategy detail page.
